testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Cargo inside a trailer must be:

options.text: Stacked no higher than three feet.
Secured so it does not move during driving.
Loaded with heavy items on top of light items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured so it does not move during driving.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be secured to prevent it from moving while driving. Loose cargo can injure the driver and other people on the road.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:
questions.explanation: When driving in fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights. Do this even during the day.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:

options.text: Press the brake pedal slowly and smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brake pedal slowly and smoothly.
questions.explanation: When stopping, press the brake pedal smoothly and gradually.

questions.question: An applicant will be denied a hazardous materials endorsement if they:
questions.explanation: Your hazardous materials endorsement can be denied or canceled if you are wanted for or convicted of certain felonies, do not have legal permanent status in the United States, are judged mentally incompetent, or are deemed a security threat by the Transportation Security Administration.

questions.question: Which of the following is a sign of a potentially drunk driver?

options.text: They stay in their traffic lane.
They drive at a consistent speed.

questions.explanation: Signs of an impaired driver include trouble staying in their lane, trouble maintaining consistent speed, or stopping without a clear reason.

questions.question: When driving a truck requiring a CDL:

options.text: You do not need to wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only if carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
You must always wear a seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: You must wear a safety belt at all times when driving a commercial motor vehicle.

questions.question: What prevents wheel lockup when braking?
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheel lockup when brakes are applied.

questions.question: When are people usually the least alert?
questions.explanation: Most drivers are the least alert late at night, especially after midnight. Crashes from tired driving happen more at night than at any other time.

questions.question: After changing a tire, the driver should stop after a short distance to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Check if rocks are in the tire tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop a short distance later to recheck that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: Where is the safety relief valve usually located?
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve in an air brake system is located in the tank that receives air first from the compressor.

questions.question: When making a tight turn, a CMV operator should:

options.text: Drive as fast as a car driver would.
Not worry about speed and just focus on the road.
Brake early and slow down gradually to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake early and slow down gradually to warn drivers behind you.
questions.explanation: Drivers behind you may not expect your CMV to slow down for a tight turn. Brake early and slow down gradually to warn them in advance.

questions.question: If you are not sure your vehicle fits under a bridge or sign, you should:
questions.explanation: If you are not certain your vehicle will fit under overhead objects, slow down and take a different route if possible.

questions.question: Before trying to put out an engine fire, you should:

options.text: Press the accelerator to use up remaining fuel.

questions.explanation: If you have an engine fire, turn off the engine as soon as you safely can. Do not open the hood when putting out the fire.

questions.question: As a truck driver carrying cargo, you are responsible for everything except:

options.text: Knowing the phone numbers of all fire departments on your route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Knowing the phone numbers of all fire departments on your route.
questions.explanation: You must inspect your cargo, recognize overloading or poor weight balance, ensure the cargo is properly secured and does not block your view, and ensure it does not restrict access to emergency equipment. You are responsible for your cargo even if someone else loaded it.

questions.question: To check automatic transmission fluid in some vehicles, the vehicle:

options.text: May need to be left running.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to be left running.
questions.explanation: For some vehicles, the engine may need to be running to check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: During an emergency stop, you should:

options.text: Veer your trailer right and stop.
Veer your trailer left and stop.

questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, use controlled braking or stab braking. Keep your vehicle in a straight line while still being able to turn if needed.

questions.question: Driving at the same speed for a long time could be a sign of distracted driving.
questions.explanation: Changing speeds is a sign of distracted driving. Keep plenty of space between you and drivers who are changing speeds.

questions.question: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must be:

options.text: A U.S. citizen or permanent resident.
Able to perform your own background check.

questions.correctAnswerText: A U.S. citizen or permanent resident.
questions.explanation: You must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident to get a hazardous materials endorsement. You will lose this endorsement if you give up your U.S. citizenship.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should use turn signals:

options.text: Only if a vehicle is close to you.

questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Do not assume other drivers will move just because you are signaling.

questions.question: If you turn to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Not brake because it could lock the wheels.
Hold the brakes down until you pass the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not brake because it could lock the wheels.
questions.explanation: Do not apply the brakes while turning to avoid a hazard. Braking while turning can lock the wheels and cause a skid.

questions.question: Looking at the speed of other vehicles helps you know when to shift to a higher gear.
questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift to a higher gear. First is engine speed (rpm). Check your manual to find the right rpm range for your vehicle and shift up when you reach the top. Second is road speed (mph). Learn which speeds work for each gear. Watch your speedometer and shift up as needed.

questions.question: A cardboard box on the road:

options.text: Should be avoided by driving off the roadway.
Will help your tires grip better.

questions.explanation: Any object on the road is potentially dangerous. Something that looks harmless, like a cardboard box or paper sack, could hold a hard or heavy object inside. This could seriously damage your vehicle.

questions.question: You are braking on dry pavement at 55 mph. How much distance does brake lag add to your total stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance for air brake vehicles has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. When braking at 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: In an emergency, you should:

options.text: Always turn on your flashers to warn others.

questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the safest choice in an emergency while driving. It is usually safer to steer around the danger to avoid a crash.

questions.question: What is brake lag?

options.text: The time it takes for brakes to work after you push the brake pedal
The distance between the brake pedal at rest and the floor
The amount of air pressure used to stop the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The time it takes for brakes to work after you push the brake pedal
questions.explanation: Air brakes cannot work instantly because air takes time to move through the brake lines. There is usually a brake lag of at least half a second between when you press the pedal and when the brakes start working. Hydraulic brakes work right away when you press the pedal.

questions.question: Items on a flatbed:

options.text: Are usually too heavy to need straps.
Do not need straps if you drive slower than 35 mph.

questions.explanation: On flatbed and open trailers, all cargo must be tied down to keep it from moving or falling off during transport.

questions.question: The posted speed limit on a ramp:

options.text: Is safe for some vehicles but may be too fast for a large truck.
Is just a suggestion and can be exceeded.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe for some vehicles but may be too fast for a large truck.
questions.explanation: Posted speeds on exit and entrance ramps are usually safe for cars. But large or heavily loaded trucks may need to drive slower than the posted speed to be safe.

questions.question: Blocking a load:

options.text: Is dangerous and should never be done.
Is only done with liquid cargo.

questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing prevent cargo from shifting while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: Before driving, you should look under your vehicle to:

options.text: See if it is on an incline.
See if it is in a parking spot.
See if it is on a decline.

questions.explanation: Before you start driving, look under your vehicle for fresh oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaks on the ground. Leaks mean your vehicle has unsafe problems.

questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher, you should:

options.text: Get as close to the fire as possible.
Stay as far from the fire as possible.
Aim at the top of the fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay as far from the fire as possible.
questions.explanation: When using a fire extinguisher, stand as far from the fire as you can. Aim at the base of the fire, not the flames. If you are unsure which extinguisher to use, especially for hazardous materials, wait for firefighters to arrive.

questions.question: Bridges usually:

options.text: Freeze only when the temperature drops well below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.
Freeze after other road surfaces freeze.

questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before the rest of the road. Be extra careful when crossing bridges if the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: If a vehicle has an inspection report, the driver should:

options.text: Ignore the report and look for problems themselves.
Take the vehicle to a mechanic.
Skip the pre-trip inspection and use only the report.

questions.explanation: Start by reading the last inspection report for your vehicle. The company should have fixed any problems listed in the report.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, you should:

options.text: Put as little weight as possible over the axles.
Spread weight evenly over the axles.
Not worry about how weight is distributed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spread weight evenly over the axles.
questions.explanation: Balance your cargo load properly. Too much weight on one axle can damage it and make steering harder. Too little weight on an axle reduces traction and causes handling problems.

questions.question: Emergency equipment, such as a fire extinguisher, is:

options.text: Only needed for vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: All commercial trucks must have the right emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red warning triangles or flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: To prevent fatigue while driving, keep the cab:
questions.explanation: Heat and poor air flow make drivers sleepy. Open windows, use vents, or turn on air conditioning to keep the cab cool and reduce fatigue.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection should:

options.text: Never be done the same way twice.
Always be done in the same order.
Only be done on sunny days.
Be skipped if the vehicle seems fine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be done in the same order.
questions.explanation: Do your pre-trip inspection the same way every time. This helps you learn the steps and ensures you do not miss anything.

questions.question: A high center of gravity:

options.text: Makes a vehicle more likely to roll over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes a vehicle more likely to roll over.
questions.explanation: A high center of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to tip over.

questions.question: In S-cam brakes, when you press the brake pedal, air pressure pushes the rod and moves the:
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air enters the brake chambers. The pressure pushes out the rods and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: Distracted drivers may be:
questions.explanation: Distracted drivers may drift between lanes, change speeds, use cell phones, look at maps or food, or talk to passengers instead of watching the road.

questions.question: Retreaded tires on a bus:

options.text: May be used anywhere on the bus.
May be used on the front.
May be used on the rear.
Cannot be used anywhere on the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be used on the rear.
questions.explanation: Retreaded tires cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus.

questions.question: The exhaust system should be:
questions.explanation: The exhaust system must be secure. All parts should be tight, not loose, broken, or missing.

questions.question: Where do you find the tire load rating?

options.text: On the inside of the driver's door
On the side of each tire

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side of each tire
questions.explanation: The tire load rating shows the maximum weight a tire can safely carry. This information is printed on the side of each tire.

questions.question: What should a driver do if their vehicle hydroplanes?

options.text: Release the accelerator and push in the clutch.
Take the vehicle out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator and push in the clutch.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, slow down by releasing the accelerator and pushing in the clutch.

questions.question: Air pressure should build up in a single air system within:
questions.explanation: In single air systems, air pressure should reach 50 to 90 psi within three minutes.

questions.question: What kind of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air brakes have three systems: service brake, parking brake, and emergency brake. Emergency and parking brakes use mechanical force.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is safe to drive on a tire missing one or two lug nuts.
A cracked lock ring on a rim is safe if you drive under 55 mph.
A missing clamp on a rim is dangerous and must be fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: A missing clamp on a rim is dangerous and must be fixed.
questions.explanation: Missing clamps, spacers, studs, or lugs are dangerous. Mismatched, bent, or cracked lock rings are also unsafe. Check that tires and rims are in good condition before driving.

questions.question: How long should oil pressure take to reach normal level when starting the vehicle?
questions.explanation: After starting the engine, oil pressure should reach normal level within seconds. Do not drive if oil pressure is low, dropping, or changing.

questions.question: A driver should always:

options.text: Travel faster than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Watch the road for hazards. Plan ahead for how to handle emergencies if they happen.

questions.question: Poor weight balance:
questions.explanation: Poorly balanced loads are unsafe and make the vehicle harder to control. Distribute cargo weight evenly when loading.

questions.question: The minimum age to apply for a CDL is 21.
questions.explanation: You must be at least 18 years old to apply for a CDL. You must be 21 to drive across state lines or to get endorsements for hazardous materials, passengers, or school buses.
